prompt: Create a vertical 3:4 intimate natural-light editorial photograph featuring a fictional, clearly adult East Asian woman, age 22. Create a distinct new fictional adult individual for this standalone portrait. The image is a quiet, candid-feeling study of a reclining woman in a floral camisole dress, with her face, loose hair and diagonal posture holding the composition. Use a slender adult frame with moderately narrow, relaxed shoulders and natural head-to-shoulder proportions, without exaggerated thinness or juvenile proportions.  FIDELITY TO THE WRITTEN SPECIFICATIONS — HIGHEST PRIORITY: Keep these fourteen visual relationships coherent: (1) a somewhat elongated adult face with a softly tapering jaw and softly rounded chin; (2) strong, gently arched dark brows above heavy-lidded eyes looking toward the camera; (3) a defined straight nose, softly full lips and a relaxed, slightly open mouth; (4) abundant long dark wavy hair fanned across the pillows with a loose off-center part and several fine strands crossing one side of her face; (5) an ivory, finely ribbed, fitted camisole dress covered in widely spaced tiny faded pink rose sprigs and muted green leaves; (6) narrow straps, a scalloped lace-trimmed V neckline and short center-front lacing below the neckline; (7) naturally shaped, securely covered torso contours flowing into the fitted waist without enlargement or flattening; (8) a diagonal reclining pose, her head and upper back resting into soft pillows; (9) one arm extended loosely to frame right along the pillow, with the other arm relaxed beside her torso; (10) a close, elevated view from above that includes her whole head and upper hips; (11) rumpled ivory floral bedding and large soft pillows that repeat the dress's small-scale floral language; (12) understated warm-grey wall panels and only a small partial bedside-table detail in the far upper left; (13) directional daylight arriving from frame right and casting readable hair and arm shadows across the pillow; (14) a low-saturation ivory, charcoal and warm-grey palette with fine photographic grain and a still, self-possessed adult expression.  Subject and styling: Give this individual a long oval face with mature facial proportions, a gently defined jaw, a small rounded chin, substantial dark brows and moderately narrow, naturally spaced eyes. The eyelids are relaxed and slightly lowered, with a subtle smudged brown lash definition rather than oversized eyes or doll-like makeup. The nose bridge is distinct and the lip shape has a soft cupid's bow and a fuller lower lip. Her head is tilted slightly, and her gaze connects with the elevated camera without a smile. Keep the lips relaxed. Her skin has a softly luminous natural warm-neutral tone under the daylight, subtle cheek warmth and delicate microtexture. Apply only light editorial retouching; preserve facial volume and the small shadow transitions around nose, eyelids and mouth. Hair is deep brown-black, thick, long and loosely waved, casually lifted at the crown and spread unevenly across the fabric. Several flyaways and strands cross the cheek and forehead, but do not hide both eyes.  Wardrobe and fabric physics: The garment is an everyday fitted ivory floral camisole dress, not a formal gown. Its fine vertical rib texture remains visible between the little faded pink and green botanical motifs. Narrow straps remain in place at both shoulders. Scalloped pale lace follows the V-shaped neckline and the curved upper edges of the bodice; short pale cross-lacing joins the center front below it. The chest is securely covered by opaque fabric. Retain a natural covered chest-to-waist line through the shaped bodice, ribbed fabric tension, diagonal recline and directional light. Do not exaggerate the anatomy or flatten the garment into a loose sack. Small horizontal and diagonal folds gather over the waist and near the lower-left edge, responding to her weight and the mattress. Keep intimate anatomy covered, without transparent panels or explicit detail.  Pose, crop and camera: Her torso travels diagonally from the lower-left area toward her head in the upper-center area. The head settles into the pillow with a slight side tilt, and the shoulder on frame right opens naturally as that arm extends outward along the pillow. The extended forearm can pass naturally out through the right edge; do not invent a hand floating beside the face. Her other arm rests alongside her body and may be partially cropped near the lower-left margin. Make the elbow and shoulder relationships physically coherent. The camera looks down from a close elevated angle, producing a personal conversational distance and a gentle diagonal perspective. Reorganize the surrounding pillow and wall space into a true vertical 3:4 frame, without stretching the person, without widening into an empty room and without cropping off the crown. Show the entire face and head, both shoulder connections and the covered upper torso through the upper hips; exclude explicit or anatomy-centered framing.  Environment and illumination: Place her on softly rumpled ivory bedding patterned with small, sparse pink flowers. Two large pillows cradle the head and raised arm, compressing naturally under the weight. The wall beyond is muted warm grey with restrained vertical panel seams; only a small soft fragment of a pale bedside table is visible at the far upper-left edge. Do not add decorative signs, lettering, recognizable place names or ornate furnishings. A single motivated window-light source from frame right makes gentle highlights on the cheek, nose, collarbone and fabric ridges, with soft but legible shadow shapes from hair and arm on the pillow. Keep the opposite side of the face softly shaded and retain the natural depth beneath the chin. Avoid flat frontal beauty lighting, icy whitening, hard artificial flash or a glossy advertising finish.  Emotional and photographic finish: The visual pull comes from her unhurried adult gaze, the close elevated viewpoint, the spread of tousled hair, the small-scale floral fabric and the believable weight of a resting posture. Preserve this stillness instead of adding an overtly provocative gesture. The face is the sharpest area; hair strands and lace have tactile detail, while the wall and table recede gently. Use delicate film-like grain, restrained contrast, subtle warm-grey color and realistic hands, limbs, contact shadows and fabric folds. The result should feel like a coherent photograph of a fictional adult, with no cartoon rendering, beauty-filter plastic skin, extra limbs, text, logos, signatures or watermarks.
